business_problem: Second Dinner relied on manual, heuristic processes for daily shop personalization, so feature iterations took about a month and recommendations lagged behind fast-changing player interests.
solution_summary: Second Dinner centralized ingest, processing, warehousing, analytics, dashboarding and machine learning on the Databricks Data + AI Platform so a small team could turn manual shop-personalization workflows into continuously updated recommendations. Player engagement and purchase data are ingested through Delta Lake and used to train ML models in MLflow, with Python logic added through PyFunk to speed experimentation across the data team. The first model produced daily population-level recommendations, then evolved into batch precomputed personalization and real-time recommendations delivered through a low-latency model-serving endpoint. Models are uploaded to the registry, retrained weekly and fed with signals about what players see, when they play and what cards they prefer, allowing the Daily Offer Shop and new bundle triggers to react to recent behavior instead of stale aggregate statistics.

data_flow: Player engagement and purchase signals land in Delta Lake on Databricks, where MLflow-managed models analyze what players see, update or buy. Recommendation outputs are then served back into Marvel Snap through the Daily Offer Shop, precomputed bundles and real-time next-best-action triggers.
business_outcome: Second Dinner moved from only 10 experiments a year to weekly iterations, sped feature launches 400%, cut model development from months to weeks and now delivers personalized shop offers and bundle recommendations that better match player behavior in real time.
